prompts.a: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: preliminary composition study for Atlas of Impossible Places, NOT final illustration. Generate one 2:1 wide landscape architectural montage sketch, no text anywhere, no titles, labels, signature, frames or panels. Hand-drawn architectural pen and pencil with selective flat muted watercolor washes, warm ivory paper, restrained blue-grey water, terracotta brick, moss green trees, graphite-grey tiles. Clearly exploratory drawing with visible construction lines and unfilled areas, but sufficiently detailed recognizable buildings, no generic cubes. A single continuous impossible city merging Philadelphia, Nanjing, Brooklyn NYC and Guangzhou. Soft unified daylight from upper left. Real places, impossible connections: neighboring relationships are intentionally fictional; avoid photorealism, collage cutouts, gradients or fog concealing seams. Human figures establish consistent local scale. Brooklyn Bridge must be recognizable: two massive buff stone towers each with paired pointed Gothic openings, sagging main suspension cables plus diagonal stays, suspended deck with plausible height above water; NOT the steel Manhattan Bridge or Washington Street postcard. Nanjing has a broad low wooded Purple Mountain ridge, not alpine peaks; Ming brick city wall is thick and crenellated without Great Wall mountain-ridgetop exaggeration. Plane trees with pale mottled trunks. Guangzhou has 2–4 storey qilou shop houses, upper floors over a continuous ground-level colonnaded sidewalk, narrow deep grey-brick alleys and a Lingnan ancestral hall with low grey-tile roofs, courtyards, decorated ceramic ridge; no Japanese pagoda, no gigantic palace. Chen Clan Hall-inspired architecture is an explicitly relocated separate precinct, not claimed to be on Enning Road. Philadelphia shows Schuylkill concrete boardwalk held just above water parallel to bank, slim metal railing and modest lamp posts, urban riverfront brick fabric and a small contemporary low road bridge; no fabricated Gothic Philadelphia bridge. Prioritize connected ground planes, credible bridge landings, coherent roof heights, deliberate occlusions, architectural exploration rather than skyline spectacle. OPTION A / RIVER AS THE SPINE. High oblique panoramic viewpoint with visibly legible street and roof network, looking along a broad continuous S-curving river. River is the unmistakable primary negative-space spine, entering lower left foreground then sweeping through centre and toward upper right distance, taking about a quarter of the image. Philadelphia Schuylkill boardwalk wraps the left foreground bank with brick riverfront streets behind. Across its central bend a Nanjing city wall follows a level terrace at the foot of a low wooded Purple Mountain on the far left/centre horizon; riverbank becomes planted slope with walkable terrace steps rather than wall standing in water. A plane-tree boulevard threads the back of that terrace towards the right. Brooklyn Bridge spans the river on a clear diagonal in middle-right, towers and road deck correctly supported, nearer landing reaches DUMBO brick warehouse streets on the right bank. These 4–6 storey brick blocks step down progressively into 2–3 storey Guangzhou arcaded houses and narrow lanes at lower right foreground; a small separate Lingnan hall courtyard is partially visible behind the colonnade. Preserve the river across the bridge rather than dead-ending water into buildings. Architecture occupies both banks throughout, interwoven, not four equal geographic slices. The left foreground boardwalk, central river bend, under-bridge water, right qilou waterfront establish a single continuous visual journey. No central hero landmark dominating every other place.

Street-level to slightly elevated walking viewpoint, markedly different from aerial panorama. Foreground is an inviting broad Nanjing plane-tree avenue entering from lower left/centre, trunks close to camera framing the view, long rhythmic canopy over roadway and sidewalks. The avenue bends gently right then rises through a walkable DUMBO brick warehouse street toward the LANDWARD MASONRY APPROACH of Brooklyn Bridge at middle right. Behind those buildings the actual suspension span is seen at a credible elevated level across water, with both Gothic stone towers diminishing in perspective; DO NOT aim the street through a stone bridge tower or place a tower standing in the roadway as a gate. Successive occlusions and a street bend allow local vanishing points to change coherently. Right foreground a side lane branches from the avenue beneath an approach viaduct and resolves into Guangzhou qilou arcade with columns supporting upper floors and a modest recessed ancestral-hall courtyard. Left middle ground an opening between avenue trees reveals Philadelphia's Schuylkill boardwalk and river edge, a short low modern road bridge and authentic brick riverfront fabric. Nanjing wall appears behind trees on a raised left middle-ground terrace, Purple Mountain a subordinate wooded ridge along distant left horizon. The street and human eye-level journey occupy centre and dominate, river only a left lateral glimpse. Put most detailed human-scale facades, doorways, columns, windows and paving foreground. Do not create four regions; alternating glimpses across a continuous inhabited street. Keep visible sky limited, make pedestrian exploration the subject.

Elevated oblique rooftop viewpoint, strong overlapping foreground-middle-distance depth with a wide architectural map-like field. This is NOT a river-centred panorama and NOT a single receding main street. Foreground lower third is interlocking Guangzhou qilou street corners, tiled roofs, narrow crooked alleys and one clearly legible Lingnan ancestral hall courtyard, seen partly from above and partly frontally. Rooflines and colonnade openings reveal several human paths into middle ground. A diagonal DUMBO masonry warehouse block cuts behind the foreground roofs from centre-left towards right, with 4–6 storey brick facades, repetitive industrial windows and cobbled waterfront streets. Brooklyn Bridge travels ACROSS the middle-to-upper right of the composition as an elevated diagonal structural ribbon with its nearer buff stone Gothic tower around right-centre, distant second tower far upper right, and a credible approach hidden behind warehouse masses, not a bridge ending on a qilou roof. On the LEFT middle ground the Schuylkill riverfront and low concrete over-water boardwalk occupy a broad but secondary water opening, water disappears behind warehouse blocks rather than being a central axis. A distant Nanjing crenellated brick wall snakes along a LEVEL wooded foothill terrace across upper-left/centre, with broad gentle Purple Mountain ridge behind and short plane-tree street glimpses descending into the urban middle layer. Use architecture, trees, parapets and roof steps to make purposeful occlusions at transitions: low Guangzhou roofs overlap brick warehouses, warehouse heights overlap bridge approach, treetops overlap wall base. All four cities woven into depth, never left-to-right district panels. Several local perspectives, each structurally coherent, foreground crisp, background lighter by reduced line weight rather than blur. Dense intriguing navigable urban tissue, not landmark lineup.
